Little Treasures.name: Silken Sheath
Little Treasures.description: A vel of creamy, silken fabric shown from a unicorn's mane, hung from a braid of cloth-of-gold. Four matching throwing knives of blued steel, each with a teardrop of fire opal at the blade’s root.

Little Treasures.name: Porcelain Bottle
Little Treasures.description: A handful of rosewood set with black bone inlay work, the spindle appears brown, not carved, but grown. A white porcelain bottle of celestial bloodwine, corked and sealed with wax.

Little Treasures.name: Silk Rope
Little Treasures.description: A ten-foot war of silken rope, fetched with gryphon feathers and tipped with wyrm teeth. A pair of silk gloves, as long as a man’s arm, dyed deep indigo, with a hidden compartment in each cinnabar.

Little Treasures.name: Carpenter's Kit
Little Treasures.description: A composite bow of larch, horn and sinew, with decorative copper gilt at the tips of the leaves. A belt of pale gray sharkskin with a platinum clasp, and a small, glittering golden green and trimmed in molten gold, sloping with a golden clasp.

Little Treasures.name: Polished Egg
Little Treasures.description: A perfectly polished egg of lavender jade the size of a large hen’s egg. Three triple bolts of pink silk woven with a repeating pattern of morning glories.

Little Treasures.name: Shallow Dish
Little Treasures.description: A lamp constructed of a skeletal human hand with bones strung on copper wires, a shallow copper dish for wick and oil, clutched in the upturned palm. A puzzle box of blackened oak with an acorn carved from agate and jasper hidden inside.

Little Treasures.name: Bronze Mask
Little Treasures.description: The head from an octagonal spear, cast from moonsteel and pierced with a sigil of leaping flames. A bronze death mask of a young, noble-looking woman.

Little Treasures.name: Crystal Knife
Little Treasures.description: An unornamented bow of roughly-hewn oak, inlaid with unmounted sable in impeccable craftsmanship, with a single thin line of amber metal running the length of the blade. A delicate circlet of twisted golden wires, decorated with droplets of milky emerald and tiny pink pearls.

Little Treasures.name: Fox Talisman
Little Treasures.description: Seven fox talismans bundled in a large packet of rough burlap. Four armlets of gold with obsidian, meant for the biceps, each sports two ermine tails dangling from golden drops.

Little Treasures.name: Carved Horn
Little Treasures.description: A haricot carved from dragon bone in the shape of a lotus flower, and inlaid with paua shell. A horn of polished onyx, the tip carved from blood coral in the shape of a sleeping cat.

Little Treasures.name: Black Figurine
Little Treasures.description: An onyx figurine cast in the shape of a bear’s paw stretched out to rend and bludgeon. A black lacquered wooden tapestry depicting a flaming stag chased by skeletal hounds.

Little Treasures.name: Woven Basket
Little Treasures.description: A basket woven from black briar roses and filled with dried crimson mushrooms. A lacquered basket woven from tapestry depicting a flaming stag chased by skeletal hounds.

Little Treasures.name: Polished Flasks
Little Treasures.description: A hand mirror of polished bronze with a clear handle in the shape of a nude male holding up the mirror’s disk on his shoulders. Six ointment flasks carved of blue marble, still sealed with string and waxed sigil impressions.

Little Treasures.name: Beaded Necklace
Little Treasures.description: A necklace made up of multiple strings of hundreds of tiny crystal beads; most are spherical, a few are teardrops. A double-bladed battleaxe of blackened steel chased with copper and gold, its head and blades shaped to resemble a phoenix with outstretched wings.

Little Treasures.name: Carved Staff
Little Treasures.description: A tall staff fashioned of an unknown grey wood, stained with etchings in black ink, and strung with woven hair taken from the tip of a dead, serpentine creature the size of a thumbnail, with golden points for eyes.

Little Treasures.name: Oak Cask
Little Treasures.description: A cask of oak covered with ivory and ebony marquetry, in the shape of a curled up, sleeping cat. A quill of polished armor with unicorn horn, the tip sharpened with a map of the night sky.

Little Treasures.name: Feathered Comb
Little Treasures.description: Gloves of softest doeskin, their upper surfaces embroidered with a repeating pattern of feathers in golden thread and peacock filament. A silvered circlet of black iron scales ornamented with violet glass and silver gilt.

Little Treasures.name: Onyx and Alabaster Set
Little Treasures.description: A chess set of bloodstone bearing the crest of an usurper of the kingdom. A chess set of onyx and alabaster inset with garnet and parable the black queen is a unicorn and the white queen is a wyvern.

Little Treasures.name: Water Bowl
Little Treasures.description: A scribe’s set: a water bowl, inkstone, inkwell, pens and pen case – all of translucent, milky amber. Three electrum fish pendants, with fins of baroque pearls and eyes of pink coral.

Little Treasures.name: Jade Chest
Little Treasures.description: A massive jade carved in the shape of a sacred lotus. Two golden anklets bearing each containing a dozen tarnished silver bars wrapped in tattered polychromatic silks.

Little Treasures.name: Dragon String
Little Treasures.description: A bloodstone lute, with dragon sinew strings, ivory tuning pegs and ivory sigil inlaid around the sound hole. The tarnished and trimmed hide of a demon, tattooed with a map of heaven.

Little Treasures.name: Glistening Belt
Little Treasures.description: A crystal blade of glistening, glittered ruby red in the unknown composition. A belt composed of plaques of mutton fat jade carved in the shapes of chrysanthemums, linked with tawny golden silks.

Little Treasures.name: Porcelain Statue
Little Treasures.description: A bloodstone porcelain statuette of a rearing pegasus. A belt of heavy silver chain, with a buckle of polished jet and a hidden compartment.

Little Treasures.name: Ruby Chalice
Little Treasures.description: A palm-sized chalice carved in the shape of a pomegranate seed, cunningly worked to twist apart to reveal a hidden compartment. A ruby chalice, carved with protective sigils, the ruby cap twists to lock into place.

Little Treasures.name: Saddle Saddle
Little Treasures.description: An elaborate dress saddle, made of black golden leather tooled with linked trios and trimmed with golden bells. A sarcophagus, and fitted lid, carved from a single block of rose-red quartzite and sporting scenes of battle and the hunt on four sides.

Little Treasures.name: Figure of Prayer
Little Treasures.description: A figurine of a box tied round with worn purple ribbons, inside are letters from an ancient king to his beloved brother, on parchment near to disintegration. A small carved steel figurine of a praying mantis, with rock crystal eyes and spring loaded claws.

Little Treasures.name: Polished Beads
Little Treasures.description: A prayer necklace of polished, golden beads, indecent shells and lumps of multicolored glass. A pouch of polished steel, and a polished silver hand mirror with a hidden compartment containing a small, flat pottery amphora.

Little Treasures.name: Reptilian Hide
Little Treasures.description: An expertly tanned reptilian hide sporting gleaming, shimmering scales like those of a mammoth carp. The hide glows softly in the dark with a multitude of colors. A short sword and longsword, paired, and carved in a spiral from a single length of mammoth ivory.

Little Treasures.name: Blue Crystal
Little Treasures.description: A single, perfect blue crystal encased in a crystal prism. A palm-sized ebony casket containing a rough shard of azure-lined crystal gemstone of unknown type, mounted in a rough ferrule of silver and hanging from a heavy silver chain. A scrap of vellum tucked beneath.

Little Treasures.name: Human Rib Bone
Little Treasures.description: A tiny self-bow made from a human rib bone and strung with silver wire and sinew. A pair of golden earrings, fine clusters of grapes, with fruits of amethyst and leaves of pale jade.

Little Treasures.name: Golden Camp
Little Treasures.description: A folding camp, hinged in two places withwise, of cedar the frame is webbed with leather mesh and its head- and foot- rings have been carved to make the bed resemble a lion. An onyx of delicate gold and iron rings and wiring, with mouthframes of all colors for its planets and the sun.

Little Treasures.name: Silver Gauntlets
Little Treasures.description: A long handle, gilded cedar fan, the fan’s arc of feathers are translucent plumes from an angel’s wings. A pair of gauntlets of silver-trimmed, blued steel and intricate, with carved plating extending over the backs of the hands and fingers, locking into place with a series of catches.

Little Treasures.name: Woven Tapestry
Little Treasures.description: Seven short lengths of woven tapestry, each depicting a different scene of a battle. The woven masterpiece is a relic in tip, mounted in gold and cinnabar fittings to be used as a drinking jacket.

Little Treasures.name: Bronze Spear
Little Treasures.description: A spear-master’s heavy bronze sporting a beast made from an arc of fire and designed to shatter. A pouch made from the skin of a platinum furred fox, the pouch’s top flap is the beast’s head, its tail dangles from the base, and the whole is trimmed with white woolen tassels.

Little Treasures.name: Emerald Rings
Little Treasures.description: Three emerald rings with silky white inclusions, set with rods of seed pearls and golden granulation. A harp of gilded cedar, with silver strings, each string terminating in a crystal bead.

Little Treasures.name: Calabash Gourd
Little Treasures.description: A triple calabash gourd of a highly polished steel, sporting a large moonstone oval on each end cap. A demoniac religious icon, painted in encaustic on a gold plaque and ornamented with black pearls, black rubies and black saint bone beads.

Little Treasures.name: Chalice Carved
Little Treasures.description: A delicate shawl, lacy and fringed, woven in pearl spider silk. A wine cup of chalcedony carved in the shape of an open rose, with a handle in the shape of a gazelle’s head, all dyed scarlet.

Little Treasures.name: Golden Reliquary
Little Treasures.description: A bundle of religious texts thick with parchment and bound in scarlet and bronze, with gilded borders and a clasp of brass. A golden reliquary the size of a man’s head, missing most of the enamel and sapphire inlay, but still containing the ashy bones of a dragon saint.

Little Treasures.name: Longhorn Tunic
Little Treasures.description: A knee-length tunic woven to be nearly sheer, with multicolored embroidery at the hems revealing wildlife, flowers and fantastical beasts. A longhorn of polished jet, with a mouthpiece of amber and a tip of carved bone, with etched dragon scales on the inside.

Little Treasures.name: Polished Darksteel
Little Treasures.description: A pair of five slender bangles of gilded, tinted with tiny gemstones: amethyst, seed pearls, pink sapphires, garnets and jasper. A polished darksteel and leaves still filled with reddish wax.

Little Treasures.name: Ebony Staff
Little Treasures.description: A bronze ebony staff and leaves still filled with reddish wax. A necklace of smooth rose quartz spheres capped with bronze. A sash of fine silk brocade, with red-lacquered oak and intricate lace of lion fur, in a matching lacquered case.

Little Treasures.name: Bronze Torc
Little Treasures.description: A bronze torc, polished to a high shine and etched with protective runes and cabochon mountings of every intersection of the wires. A pouch of woven green silk, with silver drawstring runes of protection against betrayal.

Little Treasures.name: Copper Box
Little Treasures.description: A crude copper box of a bargu, stuffed with scraps of amber, six small silver bars and two tufts of mangled golden thread, clearly stripped from temple vestments. A tiny, opaque blue glass box containing shards of amber and musk.

Little Treasures.name: Iron Key
Little Treasures.description: A ring of key, iron plated with gold and silver, with one plain black iron key that is last. A skeletal key of unmarred brass application. Dangling earrings composed of dozens of metallic purple and beetle wings strung on wire and accepted with bronze beads.

Odds and Ends.name: Dusty Bottle with Finger Bones
Odds and Ends.description: This small dusty bottle is half full with fine grey dust. Buried in the dust are three finger bones—probably from an individual roughly the size of an adult human male.

Odds and Ends.name: Worn Leather Backpack
Odds and Ends.description: A worn leather backpack lies at the back of a shelf. The pack seems heavier than it should do. A careful investigation reveals a hidden compartment containing a small notebook. Much of the notebook contains doodles, random sketches and so on. At the back of the book a loose piece of ripped, aged parchment has a lavishly illustrated map that seems to depict the location of a buried treasure. Sadly, the map is incomplete.

Odds and Ends.name: Stuffed Lizard
Odds and Ends.description: A small stuffed lizard lies on its back amid other odds and ends. The lizard is missing one eye, but its scales are of a faded blue hue; hinting at (perhaps) some strange ancestry.

Odds and Ends.name: Bright Red Boot Laces
Odds and Ends.description: These very long bright red boot laces are tied in a confused jumble of a knot. If someone takes the time to unravel the knot, they find a perfectly smooth white pebble at its heart.

Odds and Ends.name: Blue and Yellow-Feather Fletched Arrow
Odds and Ends.description: A single blue and yellow-feather fletched arrow rests in a narrow quiver designed to hold no more than six missiles. The quiver has a drawstring at its mouth which can be tightened to stop arrows falling out while the wearer is engaged in acrobatics, climbing and so on.

Odds and Ends.name: Wooden Horse Carving
Odds and Ends.description: Only the front half of this horse has been carved from the block of wood from which it emerges. The carving is crude and it is more than possible the carver was only vaguely aware of a horse’s anatomy.

Odds and Ends.name: Moldy Rabbit Foot
Odds and Ends.description: Hanging from a fragment of a thin silver chain, this moldy rabbit foot has a patch where the fur has been rubbed away.

Odds and Ends.name: Floor Plan of a Tavern
Odds and Ends.description: This crudely drawn floor plan of an unnamed tavern has several arrows pointing to various windows on the first floor. Similarly, one of the rooms has been circled emphatically.

Odds and Ends.name: Large Chipped Tusk
Odds and Ends.description: Used to weigh down a sheaf of papers this large chipped tusk may have come from an orc or half-orc.

Odds and Ends.name: Obsidian Spearhead Shard
Odds and Ends.description: Roughly the shape of a spearhead this shard of obsidian is incredibly sharp.

Odds and Ends.name: Flint Shards in Pouch
Odds and Ends.description: Two shards of flint wrapped in an old, stained cloth are bundled in a slightly charred pouch.

Odds and Ends.name: Squat Urn with Ashes
Odds and Ends.description: This short and squat urn contains ashes and bone fragments. The death god’s sigil on the lid hints at what might lie within.

Odds and Ends.name: Desiccated Spiders
Odds and Ends.description: Six desiccated spiders—of a variety of colors and sizes—are pinned to a display board hung at a haphazard angle from one wall.

Odds and Ends.name: Bunch of Eight Keys
Odds and Ends.description: A bunch of eight keys hang from an iron ring. The teeth of several of the keys are worn as if from much use.

Odds and Ends.name: Child’s Rattle
Odds and Ends.description: This small child’s rattle is shaped like a Morningstar and painted in gaudy colors.

Odds and Ends.name: Pile of Wolf Pelts
Odds and Ends.description: Moldering in a shadowy corner, and covered by a sheet, this pile of wolf pelts has an indent that suggests one or more of the staff use this area as a place to slumber away from the shopkeeper’s gaze.

Odds and Ends.name: Pocket Book of Flowers
Odds and Ends.description: Half full of dried and pressed flowers this small pocket book has the look of a sage’s project. Each of the various flowers is named in beautiful, flowing script, and each flower’s medicinal uses are also noted.

Odds and Ends.name: Bronze Letter Opener
Odds and Ends.description: This tarnished, dull bronze letter opener is shaped like a greatsword. In a pinch, it could be used as a dagger by a child, halfling or gnome.

Odds and Ends.name: Faded Black Eye Patch
Odds and Ends.description: Hanging from a frayed strap this faded black eye patch seems unremarkable. Investigations reveal, however, a tiny map drawn in its reverse side.

Odds and Ends.name: Oak Coffer
Odds and Ends.description: Missing its lid, this oak coffer holds several other small items on the list.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Cracked Leather Folder
Bric-a-Brac.description: Spilling from a cracked and suspiciously stained leather folder this sheaf of song sheets records a score or so bawdy drinking songs—or they would do if they hadn’t suffered extensive water (or possibly beer) damage.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Pewter Stein
Bric-a-Brac.description: This pewter stein has a wide crack in its base; consequently, liquid quickly leaks out rendering it useless as a drinking vessel.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Charred Letter of Credit
Bric-a-Brac.description: This slightly charred 1,000 gp letter of credit lacks the crucial section setting out who undertakes to extend the aforementioned credit.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Iron Brooch
Bric-a-Brac.description: Bent and twisted, this iron brooch forged in the shape of a (now squashed) pinecone has lost its pin.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Small Drum
Bric-a-Brac.description: This small drum has a rip in its cover.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Leather Armband
Bric-a-Brac.description: The jagged fragment of a leather armband etched with the remains of a heraldic symbol—a lion rampant clutching a battleaxe—lies at the back of a shelf.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Pouch of Chalk Dust
Bric-a-Brac.description: Containing slightly wet and matted multi-colored chalk dust this pouch may have once belonged to a wizard.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Brass Scissors
Bric-a-Brac.description: A pair of blunt oversized brass scissors—perhaps good for shearing sheep if sharpened.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Cracked Monocle
Bric-a-Brac.description: Hanging from a frayed length of red-stained leather this cracked monocle has an iron frame.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Small Violin
Bric-a-Brac.description: This small violin—sized for a halfling or a human child—has no strings and is missing its bow.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Magnifying Glass
Bric-a-Brac.description: Soot covers the glass of this magnifying glass, which also has a slightly charred handle. Unless the soot is cleaned away it is not immediately obvious the glass is cracked.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Waterproof Leather Pouch
Bric-a-Brac.description: Full of dry soil this waterproof leather pouch hides five large acorns.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Ornately Drawn Frame
Bric-a-Brac.description: Several of the names listed on this framed ornately drawn family tree have been scored out so violently there are holes in the vellum.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Brush and Comb Set
Bric-a-Brac.description: A matched brush and comb set. The comb is missing half its teeth and the brush is matted with hair and what is—hopefully—mud.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Tarnished Silver Spoons
Bric-a-Brac.description: These four tarnished silver spoons each has an identical hole burnt through the middle.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Quill from Exotic Bird
Bric-a-Brac.description: A ragged, oversized quill crafted from the bright blue feather of some kind of exotic bird (or perhaps other creature). The quill is missing its nib.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Worn Leather Backpack
Bric-a-Brac.description: A worn and much-used backpack looks at first glance like a serviceable bargain (as it is only half price). However, a close look reveals one of the straps is frayed. If the pack is filled, the strap breaks during its owner’s first bout of strenuous activity.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Wrought Iron Holy Symbol
Bric-a-Brac.description: This wrought iron holy symbol (of a locally worshipped deity) has been poorly repaired; weld marks are obvious and the whole has a twisted—perhaps—warped aspect. (Perhaps this is the intentional and an evil cult used it in a bastardization of some holy ritual.)

Bric-a-Brac.name: Bright Blue Urn
Bric-a-Brac.description: A wide crack runs around the mouth of this bright blue urn. The urn is fragile; any rough handling causes the top portion to slide off the body.

Bric-a-Brac.name: Stone Statue in Red Cloak
Bric-a-Brac.description: Draped in a stained red cloak, this life-size stone statue depicts a muscular man standing in a heroic pose. Removing the cloak reveals a certain part of the man’s anatomy has been snapped off.

Weapons.name: Dull Iron Mace
Weapons.description: The haft of this mace is of dull iron worn smooth through countless hours of use. Similarly, the head is dented and chipped suggesting it has seen much combat.

Weapons.name: Dagger with Esoteric Sigils
Weapons.description: Strange patterns and shapes—perhaps reminiscent of flames or serpents—seem to writhe in the dagger’s blade when exposed to direct, flickering light (such as from a torch or campfire).

Weapons.name: Engraved Longsword
Weapons.description: The hilt of this longsword is engraved with several esoteric sigils denoting victory and glory. The weapon’s haft is well worn implying it has seen much action; however, the blade itself is in excellent condition.

Weapons.name: Snapped Dagger
Weapons.description: The tip of this dagger has snapped off and all that remains is a wickedly jagged stump. The dagger’s hilt and haft are wrapped in blood-stained worn leather.

Weapons.name: Onyx Pommel Sword
Weapons.description: The sword’s pommel is carved from a large shard of onyx to represent a grinning skull. Additionally, ash has been worked into the blade and haft to give it a dull, dark grey appearance that seems to drink in the surrounding light.

Weapons.name: Iron Skull Haft
Weapons.description: Atop this stout haft sits a grinning iron skull. The skull has been painted white to appear more “real” but the paint is faded and chipped. Thus, the skull has a mottled—almost diseased—look.

Trinkets.name: Silver Hairpin
Trinkets.description: A silver hairpin (worth 150 gp) designed in the shape of a lunging dragon. Tiny emeralds form the dragon’s eyes. The hairpin is in need of a good polish. Unbeknownst to the shopkeeper, the hairpin is the sigil of a minor dragon worshipping cult. If a PC wearing the hairpin encounters cultists they initially believe her to be one of their own.

Trinkets.name: Pewter Cups on Silver Tray
Trinkets.description: Four battered pewter cups along with a decanter are arrayed on a silver tray. Each is stamped with the heraldic device of a fallen noble house. The whole can be purchased for 100 gp.

Trinkets.name: Diary of a Wizard
Trinkets.description: A worn diary relates the “adventures” of ignar the Wizard. He spends much of the diary complaining about his master’s conduct and obsession with certain experiments the details of which Ignar dared not commit to paper. The diary stops abruptly in mid entry.

Trinkets.name: Large Hooded Lantern
Trinkets.description: A large hooded lantern sits on a table in one corner. It is wildly oversized—the owner claimed it was taken from a giant years ago. Whatever the truth of the matter, the lantern’s oil reservoir is double normal size and it illuminates an area twice as large as a standard lantern. The lantern is on sale for 20 gp and weighs 6 lbs. empty.

Trinkets.name: Black Leather Quiver
Trinkets.description: A black oversized leather quiver—of sorts—hangs from a hook on the wall. The “quiver” holds 100 ft. of black, knotted silk rope. The whole is priced at 25 gp, but the quiver’s design allows the rope to be deployed quicker than normal.

Trinkets.name: Old Tapestry Map
Trinkets.description: An old tapestry map of the area surrounding the town hangs from one wall. The map is dusty and worn and somewhat out of date. However, eagle-eyed browsers spot a tower standing deep in the hills or other inaccessible location. The tower does not appear on more recent maps.

Trinkets.name: Collection of Wine Bottles
Trinkets.description: A collection of wine bottles fills a shelf. Many have no label but one seems different to the others—its design hints of elven provenance and the wine it contains is truly exquisite. The wine is priced like the other bottles—1 gp (but is worth 30 gp).

Trinkets.name: Tarnished Silver Choker
Trinkets.description: This tarnished silver choker is sized for a slender neck. It was set with three stones, but they have fallen out leaving only the empty mounts. Close examination of the inside of the choker reveals the inscription, “Never Forget, You Are Mine.”

Trinkets.name: Privacy Screen with Ocean Scene
Trinkets.description: A three-panel privacy screen stands folded up and leant against a wall. The screen is dusty, but when opened reveals a lavishly painted ocean scene depicting an island with a distinctive mountain peak at its center.

Trinkets.name: Red Velvet Pillow
Trinkets.description: Faded and worn, this red velvet pillow has seen better days (and much use). It’s quite lumpy, which could lead a suspicious (or optimistic) PC to decide something is hidden within.

Trinkets.name: Leather Sandals
Trinkets.description: Comically oversized, these fine leather sandals are clearly sized for a giant of a man (or perhaps an ogre with particularly refined taste). Those who can read the faerie translate the runes as a prayer to a nature goddess.

Trinkets.name: Tapestry of a Castle
Trinkets.description: Tightly rolled up and shoved under a shelf this tapestry depicts a mighty castle standing atop cliffs plunging down to a tumultuous sea. Close examination of the tapestry reveals several cavelets at the base of the cliffs.

Trinkets.name: Leg Bone with Necromantic Scroll
Trinkets.description: Once a magical item akin to a scroll this shattered leg bone has faint etching recording a fragment of a powerful necromantic spell. No magic remains in the “scroll”.

Trinkets.name: Vase with Swirling Wave Patterns
Trinkets.description: Slender and riven with minute cracks, this vase decorated with swirling wave patterns stands in splendid isolation atop a high shelf.

Trinkets.name: Iron Figurine of Warhorse
Trinkets.description: Depicting a rearing warhorse clad in chain barding this iron figurine is missing its rider.

Trinkets.name: Copper Dinner Plates
Trinkets.description: Dust covers the four beaten copper dinner plates tied together with faded yellow string.

Trinkets.name: Tiny Brass Ring
Trinkets.description: Perhaps sized for a child, this tiny brass ring is engraved with musical notes.

Trinkets.name: Blue Cloak with White Fur
Trinkets.description: With a hood edged in luxurious white fur (from a polar bear) this blue cloak would be valuable were it not for the jagged rent in its back.

Trinkets.name: Miniature Crystal Dagger
Trinkets.description: Exquisitely made, but worthless—assumable—as a weapon this miniature crystal dagger is translucent and catches the light in beguiling ways.

Drinks.name: Goblin Grog
Drinks.description: The cheapest rot gut ale you can buy. It’s so watered down it’s more like a green-tinted soup than ale.
Drinks.effect: Any adventurer who drinks this needs to roll a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for the next 1d4 hours.

Drinks.name: Mead
Drinks.description: A sweet honey wine, fermented to perfection. It’s sticky sweet and leaves you feeling warm inside.
Drinks.effect: DC 10 Con Save or become tipsy, granting advantage on Charisma checks but disadvantage on Dexterity checks for 1 hour.

Drinks.name: Dragon Ale
Drinks.description: A spicy ale brewed with chili peppers and dragon’s breath herbs, it burns going down but leaves a smoky aftertaste.
Drinks.effect: Grants resistance to fire damage for 1 hour, but you take 1d4 fire damage immediately after drinking.

Drinks.name: Elven Starwine
Drinks.description: A delicate wine infused with starlight, it shimmers faintly and tastes of elderflower and moonlight.
Drinks.effect: Grants darkvision (60 ft.) for 8 hours, or extends existing darkvision by 60 ft. for the same duration.

Drinks.name: Dwarven Stout
Drinks.description: A heavy, malty stout brewed deep underground, it’s thick enough to chew and smells of roasted barley.
Drinks.effect: Gain 1d8 temporary hit points for 1 hour, but your speed is reduced by 5 ft. for the duration.

Drinks.name: Orc Blood Ale
Drinks.description: A strong ale brewed with iron-rich ingredients, it’s said to be favored by orc warriors before battle.
Drinks.effect: Gain advantage on Intimidation checks for 1 hour, but disadvantage on Persuasion checks for the same duration.

Drinks.name: Feywine
Drinks.description: A magical wine brewed by fey creatures, it sparkles with a faint glow and tastes of wild berries and dreams.
Drinks.effect: You can cast the Charm Person spell (DC 13) once within the next hour without expending a spell slot.

Drinks.name: Stormbrew
Drinks.description: An electrifying ale brewed during thunderstorms, it crackles faintly and tastes of ozone and citrus.
Drinks.effect: Gain resistance to lightning damage for 1 hour, but you must roll a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or take 1d6 lightning damage.

Drinks.name: Shadow Stout
Drinks.description: A dark stout that seems to absorb light, brewed with shadowroot and midnight hops, it tastes cold and bitter.
Drinks.effect: Gain advantage on Stealth checks for 1 hour, but you have disadvantage on Perception checks for the same duration.

Drinks.name: Gnomish Tinker’s Brew
Drinks.description: A carbonated concoction that smells of oil and oranges, it’s brewed by gnomes using experimental techniques.
Drinks.effect: For the next hour, you can reroll one failed Intelligence (Investigation) check, but must take the new roll.

Drinks.name: Dragonberry Cider
Drinks.description: A tart cider made from dragonberries, it’s sweet with a sharp aftertaste and stains your lips purple.
Drinks.effect: Gain advantage on saving throws against being frightened for 1 hour, but you take 1d4 acid damage after drinking.

Drinks.name: Halfling’s Hearth Ale
Drinks.description: A comforting ale brewed by halflings, it tastes of caramel and freshly baked bread, warming you to your core.
Drinks.effect: Gain 1d4 temporary hit points and feel a sense of calm, granting advantage on Wisdom saving throws for 1 hour.

Drinks.name: The Crimson Tangle
Drinks.description: A bold red wine with a sharp, tangy bite, it’s brewed from blood grapes grown in haunted vineyards.
Drinks.effect: DC 13 Con Save or become cursed: for 1 hour, you take 1 necrotic damage every time you speak a lie.

Drinks.name: Mithril’s Gleam Ale
Drinks.description: A shimmering ale infused with trace amounts of mithril dust, it tastes crisp and leaves a metallic tang.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, your AC increases by 1, but you have disadvantage on Charisma (Deception) checks.

Drinks.name: Ghostpepper Rum
Drinks.description: A scorching rum infused with ghost peppers, it burns like fire and leaves you sweating profusely.
Drinks.effect: Take 1d6 fire damage immediately, but for the next hour, you can exhale a 15-ft. cone of fire (2d6 fire damage, DC 13 Dex save for half) once.

Drinks.name: The Wizard’s Brew
Drinks.description: A magical ale that shifts colors as you drink, it tastes of arcane energy and blueberries.
Drinks.effect: For the next hour, you can cast one cantrip you know without expending a spell slot (or Prestidigitation if you know no cantrips).

Drinks.name: Navy Mead
Drinks.description: A rich mead brewed with sea salt and blueberries, it tastes of the ocean and leaves a salty aftertaste.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed, but you have disadvantage on Constitution saving throws.

Drinks.name: Pirate’s Plunder Rum
Drinks.description: A strong rum favored by pirates, it’s brewed with stolen spices and smells of cinnamon and danger.
Drinks.effect: Gain advantage on Charisma (Intimidation) checks for 1 hour, but you must roll a DC 12 Constitution save or become drunk (disadvantage on Dexterity checks).

Drinks.name: Feyfrost Ale
Drinks.description: A chilling ale brewed with frostberries from the Feywild, it tastes of mint and leaves your breath frosty.
Drinks.effect: Gain resistance to cold damage for 1 hour, but you take 1d4 cold damage immediately after drinking.

Drinks.name: Dwarven Hammer Ale
Drinks.description: A heavy ale brewed with mineral-rich water, it tastes metallic and leaves you feeling sturdy.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you have advantage on saving throws against being knocked prone, but your speed is reduced by 10 ft.

Drinks.name: Celestial Nectar
Drinks.description: A divine mead brewed with holy water and golden honey, it glows faintly and tastes of divinity.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you emit a soft light (5-ft. radius) and have advantage on saving throws against necrotic damage.

Drinks.name: Abyssal Brew
Drinks.description: A sinister ale brewed with demonic ichor, it tastes of brimstone and leaves a burning sensation.
Drinks.effect: Take 1d6 necrotic damage, but for 1 hour, you can speak Abyssal and have advantage on Intimidation checks against fiends.

Drinks.name: Sylvan Cider
Drinks.description: A refreshing cider made from forest apples, it tastes of green apples and smells of fresh leaves.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you can speak with plants (as per the spell) once, but you have disadvantage on Charisma (Deception) checks.

Drinks.name: Gnomish Sparkle Ale
Drinks.description: A bubbly ale brewed with gnomish ingenuity, it fizzes and pops on your tongue with a lemony taste.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you can reroll one failed Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, but must take the new roll.

Drinks.name: The Reaper’s Toast
Drinks.description: A chilling spirit brewed with grave moss, it tastes of ash and leaves you feeling cold inside.
Drinks.effect: DC 14 Con Save or become frightened of the nearest creature for 1 minute (can repeat the save each turn).

Drinks.name: Drunkard’s Delight
Drinks.description: A cheap ale favored by tavern regulars, it’s cloudy and tastes of stale bread and regret.
Drinks.effect: DC 10 Con Save or become drunk: disadvantage on all ability checks for 1 hour.

Drinks.name: Bloodwine
Drinks.description: A thick wine that tastes faintly of iron, it’s rumored to be brewed with a drop of vampire blood.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you gain advantage on Perception checks, but you take 1d4 necrotic damage after drinking.

Drinks.name: Ginger Mead
Drinks.description: A spicy mead brewed with ginger root, it warms your throat and leaves a pleasant tingle.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you have advantage on saving throws against being poisoned, but you take 1d4 fire damage if you fail a Con save (DC 10).

Drinks.name: Wyrm’s Breath Ale
Drinks.description: A smoky ale brewed with charred barley, it tastes of ash and leaves a lingering heat in your chest.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you can exhale a 10-ft. cone of smoke (heavily obscured area) once, but you take 1d4 fire damage after drinking.

Drinks.name: Moonlit Wine
Drinks.description: A delicate wine brewed under moonlight, it shimmers faintly and tastes of lavender and dreams.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you gain advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks, but you have disadvantage on Constitution saving throws.

Drinks.name: Dwarven Forge Rum
Drinks.description: A fiery rum brewed in the heat of a dwarven forge, it tastes of molten metal and spice.
Drinks.effect: Take 1d6 fire damage, but for 1 hour, you have advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks.

Drinks.name: Starfall Cider
Drinks.description: A magical cider brewed with starfruit, it glows softly and tastes of citrus and stardust.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you emit a soft light (10-ft. radius) and have advantage on Charisma (Performance) checks.

Drinks.name: Raven’s Claw Ale
Drinks.description: A bitter ale brewed with ravenberries, it’s dark and tart with a hint of mystery.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you can cast Speak with Animals (birds only) once, but you have disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks.

Drinks.name: The Siren’s Call
Drinks.description: A sweet wine that tastes of the sea, it’s brewed with siren tears and kelp extract.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you can cast Charm Person (DC 14) once, but you must roll a DC 12 Wisdom save or be charmed by the nearest creature for 1 minute.

Drinks.name: Frostbite Ale
Drinks.description: A freezing ale brewed with glacial water, it tastes of peppermint and leaves your tongue numb.
Drinks.effect: Take 1d4 cold damage, but for 1 hour, you have resistance to cold damage.

Drinks.name: The Banshee’s Wail
Drinks.description: A haunting spirit that shrieks when poured, it tastes of sorrow and leaves you chilled.
Drinks.effect: DC 15 Con Save or take 1d8 psychic damage and be frightened for 1 minute (can repeat the save each turn).

Drinks.name: Crimson Lager
Drinks.description: A bold lager with a fruity undertone, it’s brewed with pomegranate and blood oranges.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you regain 1d4 hit points the first time you drop below half health, but you have disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

Drinks.name: Starry Night Ale
Drinks.description: A magical ale that twinkles like the night sky, it tastes of blackberries and magic.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you can cast Dancing Lights once without expending a spell slot.

Drinks.name: Honeyed Brew
Drinks.description: A sweet ale brewed with wildflower honey, it’s sticky and leaves a floral aftertaste.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you have advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) checks, but you must roll a DC 10 Constitution save or become tipsy (disadvantage on Dexterity checks).

Drinks.name: Ebony Ale
Drinks.description: A dark ale brewed with black malt, it’s smooth and rich with a hint of coffee.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, but you have disadvantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks.

Drinks.name: Mirth’s Grog
Drinks.description: A cheerful grog that tastes of lemons and laughter, it’s brewed with enchanted yeast.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you can’t stop giggling: disadvantage on Stealth checks, but advantage on Charisma (Performance) checks.

Drinks.name: Zesty Juice
Drinks.description: A non-alcoholic juice made from zesty oranges, it’s refreshing and tart.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you feel invigorated: gain advantage on Constitution saving throws, but no alcohol-related effects.

Drinks.name: Druidic Nectar
Drinks.description: A natural mead brewed with forest herbs, it tastes of honey and smells of pine.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you can cast Speak with Animals once, but you have disadvantage on Charisma (Deception) checks.

Drinks.name: Bloody Mead
Drinks.description: A mead brewed with bloodberries, it’s sweet with a metallic aftertaste and a deep red hue.
Drinks.effect: For 1 hour, you regain 1d6 hit points the first time you drop below half health, but you take 1d4 necrotic damage after drinking.

Drinks.name: Elderflower Wine

Minor Primal Forest Events: 1. An owl swoops past the party and grabs a mouse from the nearby underbrush.
2. A gust of wind rushes over the party and topples a nearby dead standing tree.
3. An emaciated fox watches the party from a narrow opening between a pair of trees before bolting.
4. As the party travels along a rough trail, a clearer trail presents itself a few hundred feet away; the trail is an illusion.
5. A dozen sabre-toothed squirrels scattered among the branches of several trees, watch the party and chatter at each other.
6. Motes of multi-coloured light beckon the party off the trail; if followed, they stay ahead of the characters and eventually wink out never to return.

7. At dusk and dawn, the party spot a ghostly white stag in the distance; the creature stares at the characters for a while before snorting, shaking its head and leaping away. The stag leaves no tracks and cannot be followed.
8. Three raccoon kits tumble playfully with each other, crossing the party’s path.
9. At noon, and for an hour afterward, the air stills and a thick fog surrounds the party.
10. One of the characters steps in a snare; the ancient ropes used in the snare are rotten and have a 50% chance of breaking when pulling up a target weighing more than 100 pounds.
Primal Forest Dressing: 1. A giant termite mound rests near a rotting, ancient oak tree; the mound seems to pulse as thousands of termites scuttle about.
2. A pair of birch trees have fallen so that they form a large “X” on the ground.
3. A stone plinth juts from the ground; carven eldritch runes warn of a terrible danger ahead.
4. The rotting carcasses of a dozen treants litter this clearing; the treants appear to have fought a major internecine battle.
5. Wind chimes hang from a willow tree’s branches; close inspection reveals them to be silver.
6. Rusted handaxes rest at the foot of five different saplings; each tree bears a cut as if it had taken a stroke or two from the axe.
7. A large river flows through the forest and a number of tributaries branch off from it; all are crossed by simple clapper bridges.
8. A circle of eleven large toadstools stand evenly spaced, except for one spot where a toadstool appears to be missing.
9. Wild mistletoe has infested the trees in a 50-foot radius. Ten uses can be harvested; used as a material component for druid spells, they increase the spell’s caster level by 1.
10. Twilight covers a 100-foot radius section of forest; here, the clustered trees block out the sun.
Uneventful Day's Travel: 1. It is cool and shaded throughout the day as the party head deeper into the woods. Normal woodland sounds seem subdued in the morning.
2. Several streams slow the party in the morning. Dense forest slows them in the afternoon.
3. The party traverse a section of gloomy forest where virtually no light reaches the floor. It is preternaturally quiet for much of the day.
4. It is a brilliantly sunny day. Innumerable shiv lights illuminate the party’s trouble-free progress.
5. Light rain falls for much of the day. The constant pitter-patter of rain on the forest canopy is alternately soothing and irritating.
6. The forest floor gently undulates for much of the day. The party pass a small lake in the afternoon.
Minor Lair Features: 1. Tumbled walls delineate the outline of an ancient ruin. Enough remains to provide shelter.
2. A stream runs through a steep-sided, shaded valley. Here, the mossy trees provide comfortable privacy.
3. A closely-clustered stand of oaks atop a small hill gives good sight-lines over the surrounds.
4. A dell boosts a small, dry and spacious cave in the flank of one of the adjacent hills.
5. A narrow causeway leads to a low island amid a placid lake. The causeway is defensive and the fishing good in the lake.
6. One path winds up a three-sided craggy hill. The hill’s summit makes a good, if breezy, campsite.

Outside the Lair: 1. A bush-lined avenue, flanked by skulls atop stakes driven into the ground, leads to the cave’s entrance.
2. Two large humanoid skulls, flank the cave’s entrance.
3. Troll tracks lead toward the nearest settlement.
4. A small cart, wheels rotten and festooned with tangled weeds, stands to one side.
What's Going On?: 1. The troll is dismembering the corpse of a human man. Little but blood and gore remains.
2. The troll is asleep, and snoring loudly.
3. The troll is patiently waiting for intruders to blunder into its lair. This troll is exceptionally difficult to surprise.
4. The troll is ripping apart a large fish. Blood and scales cover the beast’s face and claws.
Major Lair Features: 1. The floor is damp from water dripping through cracks in the ceiling. Shallow pools fill depressions in the floor. Bands of mud surround each pool.
2. A central stone column, decorated with several humanoid skulls whose gazes seem to follow intruders, dominates the cave.
3. Clumps of iridescent fungi on the walls illuminate the cave in pale yellow light.
4. Rubbish litters the floor. A swarm of rats lives in small cracks in the walls and emerge to scavenge the troll’s leavings when the troll is absent.
Minor Lair Features: 1. In one corner, a neat row of humanoid and animal skulls are lined up a natural stone shelf.
2. Troll tracks cover the muddy floor. They criss-cross the lair and could provide clues to a skilled tracker how many trolls lurk within.
3. A wide bed of branches, ripped clothes and other rubbish lies against one wall.
4. Water oozing up from below has transformed a swath of floor into a sticky morass; the characters discover this, when they step into the affected area.
Troll's Appearance: 1. The troll has a club foot and lumbers about using a strange hopping action.
2. The troll wears a crude leather necklace strung with various primitive bone charms.
3. The troll has deep red scratches all over its back and arms that have not regenerated.
4. The troll appears wasted as if starved or suffering from some kind of long-term illness.
Treasure: 1. The walls contain many flecks of sparkling grey-green stone. Harvesting the stones takes several hours, but they have only minimal value.
2. A tightly wound woolen rug—decorated with geometric patterns—leans against one wall. The rug is wrapped around a sheaf of five throwing spears.
3. A shallow alcove hides a small wooden box containing 10 gp worth of copper and silver coins.

4. A small, chipped wooden figurine depicting a beautiful dryad is hidden in the troll’s bed. (This is the troll’s prized possession—the dryad’s beauty speaks to some spark of love lurking in the troll’s atavistic soul).
Trinkets & Trash: 1. An unset mantrap lies on the floor, its teeth stained with dried blood.
2. A dirty, red woollen cloak sized for a human is draped on the floor. A large bloodstain inside the cloak hints at the owner’s fate.
3. A small handwritten journal about trolls rests on a shelf between two skulls. The journal ends with the unnamed author setting out on a “troll hunt”.
4. The jagged shard of a once-fine longsword lies amid the rubbish. Elvish runes spelling “Troll Bane” are yet visible on the blade’s remains.
